# VS Code Setup for Scripture Pipelines Projects

Recommended settings and the privacy/convenience trade-offs for AI-assisted pipeline work.

## Recommended settings.json

Copy the block below into `.vscode/settings.json` (create the file if it doesn't exist).
Adjust to taste — the comments explain each section.

```json
{
  "files.trimTrailingWhitespace": true,
  "editor.largeFileOptimizations": false,

  // Prevent VS Code from offering to open parent folders as a workspace,
  // which can confuse Copilot about which repo it is in.
  "git.openRepositoryInParentFolders": "never",

  // Stack chat sessions vertically so long conversations are easier to scroll.
  "chat.viewSessions.orientation": "stacked",

  // --- Terminal auto-approve ---
  // Controls which commands Copilot can run in the terminal WITHOUT prompting.
  // Read the privacy section below before enabling anything beyond the defaults.
  "chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove": {

    // Safe read-only commands — approve freely.
    "pwd": true, "ls": true, "dir": true, "echo": true,
    "cat": true, "head": true, "tail": true, "wc": true,
    "nl": true, "grep": true, "rg": true, "find": true,
    "sort": true, "column": true, "date": true,
    "basename": true, "dirname": true, "which": true,
    "file": true, "stat": true,

    // Read-only git commands — approve.
    "/^git\\s+status\\b/": true,
    "/^git\\s+log\\b/": true,
    "/^git\\s+show\\b/": true,
    "/^git\\s+diff\\b/": true,
    "/^git\\s+ls-files\\b/": true,
    "/^git\\s+grep\\b/": true,
    "/^git\\s+branch\\b$/": true,

    // Commands that change state — keep at false (require confirmation).
    "rm": false, "rmdir": false, "del": false,
    "curl": false, "wget": false,
    "chmod": false, "chown": false,
    "kill": false, "ps": false,

    // Scripting / eval — always false.
    "xargs": false, "eval": false, "jq": false
  }
}
```

## Privacy vs. convenience

`chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` is a direct trade-off:

**More approvals = less friction, more exposure.**

| Risk | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Read commands are safe** | `ls`, `cat`, `grep` etc. only read from your disk. Approving them just saves a click. |
| **Write/delete commands are not** | `rm`, `del` can destroy work. Always require confirmation. |
| **Network commands are not** | `curl`, `wget`, `Invoke-WebRequest` can exfiltrate data or download malicious payloads. Always require confirmation. |
| **`eval` / `Invoke-Expression` are never safe** | These can run arbitrary generated code without any further prompt. Never approve. |
| **`cd` is subtle** | Changing directory mid-session can cause Copilot to operate in the wrong scope. Leave at false. |

**The recommended config above approves only read-only commands.** This eliminates most confirmation dialogs during normal pipeline development (reading files, checking git status) while keeping every state-changing operation behind a prompt.

If you are working on a project with sensitive content (Bible translations, proprietary data), be aware that even read-only auto-approval means Copilot can scan any file in the workspace and include it in its context window. That is intentional for pipeline development but worth understanding.
